subsystems.name: Sensing layer
subsystems.role: gathers real-time data from the city.
parts: smart meters and building management systems

subsystems.name: Connectivity and compute
subsystems.role: moves and processes the data stream.

subsystems.name: 3D city model
subsystems.role: the geometric and semantic replica of the built environment.

subsystems.name: Simulation engines
subsystems.role: model how the city behaves under different conditions.

subsystems.name: Integration and API layer
subsystems.role: connects live data to models and applications.

subsystems.name: User interface and decision support
subsystems.role: lets planners and operators see and act on the twin.

buildSteps.title: Define scope and governance
buildSteps.detail: Decide which systems (traffic, energy, water) the twin will cover, and set rules for data ownership, access and privacy.

buildSteps.title: Capture static geometry
buildSteps.detail: Aircraft or drones with LiDAR scan the city; ground surveys fill gaps; data is processed into a 3D mesh.

buildSteps.title: Deploy sensor network
buildSteps.detail: Install or connect IoT devices: traffic counters, air-quality monitors, smart meters, and building sensors.

buildSteps.title: Build the data pipeline
buildSteps.detail: Stream sensor data into a cloud platform with storage, cleansing, and time-stamping so it can be used in real time.

buildSteps.title: Create the semantic model
buildSteps.detail: Tag buildings and infrastructure with attributes (use, age, materials) so simulations can reason about them.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate simulations
buildSteps.detail: Run models against recorded events (e.g. a past flood or rush hour) and adjust until they match reality.

buildSteps.title: Integrate and visualize
buildSteps.detail: Connect models to a 3D engine and dashboards so users can explore scenarios in real time.

buildSteps.title: Operate and update
buildSteps.detail: Keep the twin live by streaming data, updating geometry when buildings change, and re-calibrating periodically.

prerequisites.why: cities have some sensors but not comprehensive coverage of all relevant systems.
5G and fibre enable real-time data flow from sensors to compute.
mature engines can render large city models with reasonable performance.
provide the compute and storage for simulations and data streams.
cities use many incompatible formats and protocols, making integration hard.
needed to use personal data (e.g. mobility traces) without violating privacy.

pathway.milestone: district-scale digital twins for specific domains (traffic, energy) in pilot projects, such as Singapore's Virtual Singapore and the EU's Destination Earth
pathway.unlocks: better understanding of data integration and simulation accuracy.

pathway.milestone: city-wide integrated twins that combine multiple domains
pathway.unlocks: real-time control of traffic signals and energy demand, improving efficiency and reducing emissions.

pathway.milestone: predictive twins for climate resilience and disaster response
pathway.unlocks: simulate floods, heatwaves and evacuations before they happen, saving lives and reducing damage.
AI systems that continuously optimize city operations with human oversight, creating more responsive and sustainable cities.
